title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.24005v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Native multimodal large language models (native MLLMs) jointly encode visual and linguistic sequences within a unified autoregressive Transformer, emerging as a promising paradigm for multimodal understanding. Unlike conventional ViT-based MLLMs relying on external vision encoders, ViT-free native MLLMs tokenize pixel patches directly, potentially suffering severe visual token redundancy. A pilot study confirms this: unlike ViT-based models that degrade under compression, ViT-free MLLMs tolerate aggressive compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. Yet existing compression methods target ViT-based settings, leaving native MLLMs, which stand to gain the most, unexplored. To close this gap, we introduce an analysis pipeline centered on token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy, revealing that (i) redundancy is distributed independently and heterogeneously along height and width axes,

translated_title: PACE：面向高效原生多模态大模型的帕累托自适应压缩
translated_abstract: 原生多模态大语言模型在统一的自回归Transformer中联合编码视觉与语言序列，正成为多模态理解领域一种颇具前景的范式。与依赖外部视觉编码器的传统基于ViT的MLLM不同，无ViT的原生MLLM直接对像素块进行分词，因此可能存在严重的视觉token冗余。一项先导性研究证实了这一点：与压缩后性能下降的基于ViT的模型不同，无ViT的MLLM能够容忍激进的压缩，且性能几乎无损甚至有所提升。然而，现有的压缩方法均针对基于ViT的设置，而最有望从压缩中获益的原生MLLM却尚未被探索。为填补这一空白，我们提出了一个以token可辨别性和跨维度异构冗余为核心的分析流程，并揭示了：(i) 冗余在高度与宽度两个维度上呈独立且异构的分布，……
tldr: 提出PACE，一种帕累托自适应压缩方法，通过分析token可辨别性与跨维度异构冗余，为无ViT原生多模态大模型实现高效且近乎无损的视觉token压缩。
en_tdlr: PACE, a Pareto-adaptive compression method that leverages token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy to enable efficient, near-lossless visual token compression for ViT-free native MLLMs.
